papers.title: Axioms for relative entropy
papers.abstract: For normal states of arbitrary von Neumann algebras, we characterize positive finite multiples of Araki relative entropy among non-degenerate divergences. The axioms are monotonicity under normal unital completely positive maps, tensor additivity, superadditivity for product second states, and separate lower semicontinuity in the predual norm. Alternatively, a conditional-expectation identity replaces the two tensor assumptions. The proof uses order bounds and asymptotic estimates on tensor powers. An appendix proves the known analytic estimates needed here, using standard modular theory and Haagerup L^p spaces. We also obtain the corresponding characterization in the C* algebraic setting.

papers.title: An isolated complex Hadamard matrix with nonzero defect
papers.abstract: We exhibit a complex Hadamard matrix of nonzero defect which is isolated among complex Hadamard matrices, up to Hadamard equivalence. This counterexample is realized by a Butson-type Hadamard matrix of size $13$, with entries roots of order $6$ of unity. In the language of commuting squares, this shows that the span condition, previously introduced by the second author as a sufficient condition for isolation, is not a necessary condition for isolation.

papers.title: Polynomial growth and dynamic asymptotic dimension
papers.abstract: We show that principal ample groupoids with local polynomial growth of degree at most $s$ have dynamic asymptotic dimension at most $\lfloor s\rfloor$. As a consequence, $\sigma$-compact principal ample groupoids with local polynomial growth have slow dynamic asymptotic dimension growth.

papers.title: A Counterexample to Voiculescu's Normal Dilation Conjecture
papers.abstract: We construct a compact operator $T$ with trace class self-commutator and vanishing Helton-Howe measure such that $T\oplus S-M\notin \mathcal{S}_2$ for every bounded operator $S$ and every bounded normal operator $M$. This gives counterexamples to Voiculescu's normal dilation and stable classification conjectures. The construction uses magnetic shifts on finite square tori. Their real parts have commutators of uniformly bounded trace norm, while their frame errors admit logarithmic lower bounds in the lattice size. A summability criterion for frame error turns these finite-dimensional estimates into a compact counterexample. The same operator inequalities yield a rank profile invariant under Hilbert-Schmidt perturbations and normal stabilization, which distinguishes the example from zero.

papers.title: Matricial stability and central corrections for generalized Jordan derivations on amenable $C^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: We study norm stability of third-type generalized Jordan identities, allowing their auxiliary maps to be arbitrary. A canonical normalization eliminates these witnesses with a factor of four. For a unital $C^*$-algebra and a unital contractive Banach bimodule, the zero-defect maps are precisely sums of a derivation and multiplication by a central module element. We characterize scalar stability by the closed range of the normalized Jordan-defect operator. For operator bimodules, two explicit $2\times2$ tests recover an ordered Leibniz defect and a commutator defect. If the algebra has an approximate diagonal bounded by $M$ and the module is weak$^*$ closed, these tests yield approximation by an inner derivation plus a central multiplier with error at most $8M$ times the normalized matrix defect. The corresponding completely bounded estimate holds at all matrix levels. For full matrix algebras the constant is $8$, independently of their size, and weak$^*$ closedness is unnecessary. When the map vanishes at the identity, the constants improve to $2M$ and $2$, respectively.

papers.title: Scaling Fourier Inequalities for Locally Compact Quantum Groups
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study Fourier and convolution inequalities on locally compact quantum groups in the presence of the scaling group. For $1\le p\le 2$, we investigate a family of scaling Fourier transforms and the associated norms $H_{p,\theta}(\mathbb G)$, and we show that $H_{p,\theta}(\mathbb G)<1$ for the real quantum $az+b$ group and $0<\theta<1$, $1<p<2$. We also investigate scaling convolution for locally compact quantum groups and, by extending the ordinary convolution, obtain the corresponding scaling Young inequality in four different regions. In Young Region~II, under $1<p,s<2$ and $2\leq r<\infty$, we construct sequences proving norm one at every effective vertex and prove strict inequality at every other effective point.

papers.title: Diagonal and Fine Tower Dimensions for Minimal Circle Homeomorphisms and Product Actions
papers.abstract: We study minimal circle homeomorphisms and their products with Cantor systems, and show that these actions have diagonal dimension at most two and fine tower dimension at least two. Consequently, diagonal dimension, fine tower dimension, and tower dimension are all equal to two for minimal circle homeomorphisms. We also obtain a strict separation between tower dimension and fine tower dimension on a one-dimensional space.

papers.title: Property A and the identification of the maximal and reduced uniform Roe algebras
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a discrete metric space of bounded geometry. We prove that $X$ has property A if and only if the canonical map $$\lambda:C^*_{u,max}(X)\to C^*_u(X)$$ is an isomorphism.

papers.title: Sharp $L_p$-Regularity for Quantum Markov Semigroups
papers.abstract: We determine the sharp universal constants in positive-input $L_p$-regularity for finite-dimensional quantum Markov semigroups with a faithful invariant state. For $1<p<\infty$, they are $p\sin(\pi/p)/(2(p-1))$ under KMS symmetry and $\frac{p}{2(p-1)}\tan(\frac{\pi}{2}\min\{1/p,1-1/p\})$ without a symmetry assumption, with the endpoint values at $p=1$ given by $\pi/2$ and $\pi/4$, respectively.

papers.title: Structural and Dynamical Properties of Subfactor Commuting Squares
papers.abstract: This paper explores the algebraic invariants and ergodic behavior of the finite-index inclusions forming commuting squares of $\text{II}_1$ factors. We begin by establishing how regularity, intermediate-subfactor lattices, and Weyl groups transfer across the commuting square under relative commutant and irreducibility conditions. Furthermore, we provide a complete characterization, via a novel factorization theorem, of the unitary normalizers of the upper inclusion when the lower inclusion is regular. Applying these findings to crossed-product inclusions induced by discrete groups, we introduce a relative eigenbasis property that preserves regular inclusions. Finally, we contrast this by proving that a relative weak mixing condition on the group action forces the crossed-product inclusion to be singular.

papers.title: Operator-valued maximal $f$-divergences for completely positive maps
papers.abstract: We introduce an operator-valued maximal $f$-divergence for completely positive (CP) maps between von Neumann algebras, associated with an operator convex function $f$ on $(0,+\infty)$. The construction takes values in the extended lower-semibounded self-adjoint part of the codomain von Neumann algebra. We prove independence of the common CP upper bound used in its computation, joint subadditivity, monotonicity under unital precomposition and normal postcomposition, a martingale convergence theorem for normal CP maps, and joint lower semicontinuity in the point-$\sigma$-weak topology. For normal positive functionals, our construction recovers Hiai's maximal $f$-divergence. As a consequence, we establish its joint weak lower semicontinuity for arbitrary von Neumann algebras, answering a question left open by Hiai. For $\eta(t)=t log t$, we obtain an operator-valued Belavkin--Staszewski (BS) relative entropy. Moreover, for normal channels with $\sigma$-finite codomain, we prove that the BS channel divergence of Hollands and Ranallo coincides with the extended norm of our operator-valued divergence. Finally, we give finite-dimensional examples and obtain an explicit formula for a finite-index conditional expectation. In the BS case, this formula reduces to the logarithm of the Jones--Kosaki index.

papers.title: Noncommutative extensions of an ergodic theorem of Breiman
papers.abstract: Let $(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ be a tracial von Neumann algebra, $T:L_1(\mathcal{M},\tau)\to L_1(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ be induced by a normal $\tau$-preserving $*$-automorphism of $\mathcal{M}$, and $x\in L_1(\mathcal{M},\tau)$. We will prove the bilaterally almost uniform convergence of averages of the form $$\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}T^k(x_k),$$ generalizing an ergodic theorem proven by Breiman in \cite{Breiman57}, where $(x_k)_{k=0}^{\infty}$ is an element of the noncommutative vector-valued $L_p$-space $L_p(\mathcal{M},\tau;\ell_\infty)$ such that there exists $x\in L_p(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ with $(x_k-x)_{k=0}^{\infty}\in L_p(\mathcal{M},\tau;c_0)$. A generalization to semifinite $(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ and general positive Dunford-Schwartz operators $T\in DS^+(\mathcal{M},\tau)$ is shown as well when $1<p<\infty$. In addition to these, we also prove a number of generalizations of the results to weighted, subsequential, and other types of averages.

papers.title: Finite-summability in the noncommutative geometry of crossed products
papers.abstract: We study finite-summability of unbounded representatives of $K$-homology classes for crossed-product $C^*$-algebras associated with actions on compact spaces. Using Kasparov's Dirac--dual-Dirac method, we isolate geometric conditions on the $\gamma$-element under which elements of $K$-homology can be transferred to a crossed product associated with a proper action and represented by finitely summable unbounded cycles defined from Dirac-type operators with an unbounded potential. We relate finite-summability of these operators to integrability properties of the potential by spectral estimates for Schr\"odinger operators on manifolds of bounded geometry. In particular, for finitely generated nilpotent groups this leads to finitely summable, unbounded representatives of all $K$-homology classes. We also give examples showing that representability of $K$-homology classes by finitely summable unbounded cycles is not invariant under $KK$-equivalence.

papers.title: Entropy of Noncommutative Spaces
papers.abstract: We give an overview of the second quantisation of spectral triples and compute the entropy of the noncommutative space described by it in terms of a spectral action. This reviews earlier work by Chamseddine, Connes and the second author, but presented here concisely, including the procedure of second quantisation using infinite-dimensional Clifford algebras. We exemplify the theory by considering noncommutative metric spaces consisting of $N$ points. The entropy of these discrete spaces is explicitly computed, and we study the resulting entropic force as well as the evolution of the spaces in time.

papers.title: The Powers-St{\o}rmer-Ogata inequality for operator monotone functions
papers.abstract: We show that for any positive operator monotone function $f$ the inequality $\int_{[0,\infty)} f(t) \, \mathrm{d} \left\lVert E^{\Delta_{\varphi,\psi}}(t) \xi_\psi \right\rVert^2 + f'_\infty \varphi(1-s(\psi)) \geq \frac{f(1)}{2} \Bigl( \varphi(1) + \psi(1) - \lVert \varphi - \psi \rVert \Bigr)$ holds, where $\varphi, \psi \in \mathcal{M}_{*,+}$ are two normal positive linear functionals on a von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{M}$, and $\Delta_{\varphi,\psi}$ is the associated relative modular operator. Choosing $f(t) = t^s$ with $s \in [0,1]$, the Powers-St{\o}rmer-Ogata inequality is recovered.

papers.title: Rank-One HCIZ Integrals and Multiplicative Convolutions
papers.abstract: We study how spectral averaging interacts with the logarithm in large-dimensional rank-one Harish-Chandra--Itzykson--Zuber (HCIZ) integrals. For independent bi-unitarily invariant matrices $A,B$ with uniformly bounded deterministic singular values and weakly convergent empirical spectral measures of their Gram matrices, the integral for $(BA)^*(BA)\otimes\mathbf{1}_N$ has two limiting descriptions at speed $N^2$ for small real parameters: averaging its logarithm gives free multiplicative convolution, whereas taking the logarithm after averaging gives classical multiplicative convolution. We also prove an exact finite-dimensional equality between this annealed integral and the one for $(A^*A)\otimes(B^*B)$. For any fixed $k\ge3$ factors under the hypotheses stated for $A,B$, the annealed limits at speed $N^k$ generally differ for small positive parameters, and we characterize the equality cases. For tensor products with any fixed number $k$ of factors, global Haar vectors at speed $N^k$ and product-state vectors at speed $N$ yield classical and free multiplicative convolution, respectively, for small real parameters under the corresponding hypotheses. We also derive the known multiplicativity of the $S$-transform.

papers.title: A Quantum Metric Approach to Stabilizer Codes
papers.abstract: We associate a spectral triple with each stabilizer code in a projective error model arising from a nice error basis and equipped with a length function. The spectral triple records the dimension of the code as well as the minimum code distance. For Pauli stabilizer codes of dimension greater than one with Hamming weight, Latr\'emoli\`ere's dual propinquity provides a pseudometric which allows us to compare codes of different physical and logical dimensions. We show that in the resulting topology, minimum distance of a code is locally constant for qubits and for qudits of dimensions three and five. Thus correction of all errors up to a prescribed weight is a local property in these cases. Moreover, for each prime $p$, we classify the underlying $C^*$-algebras in the metric closure as a subclass of AF algebras, namely those arising as tensor products of $C((\mathbb{Z}_p)^r)$, for $r \in \{0,1,2, \ldots , \infty\}$, with matrix algebras of $p$-power order or the UHF algebra of type $p^\infty$. Every such $C^*$-algebra not isomorphic to $M_{p^k}(\mathbb{C})$ for any $k\geq 1$ occurs as the underlying algebra of a point in the metric boundary. In particular, we obtain the CAR algebra as a metric limit of qubit stabilizer codes.

papers.title: Quantum Gromov--Hausdorff Convergence of Spectral Truncations for Amenable Discrete Quantum Groups with Modified Rapid Decay
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be an amenable discrete quantum group with the modified rapid decay property relative to a proper central length $\ell$. We construct a modularly corrected commutator seminorm on $C_r^*(G)$ and prove its right invariance. Averaging over the coproduct yields a regular bi-invariant Lip-norm. For the spectral projections $P_R=\chi_{[0,R]}(D_\ell)$, we equip the finite-dimensional operator systems $A_R=P_RC_r^*(G)P_R$ with the Lip-norms induced by the compressed left and right coactions. We prove quantum Gromov--Hausdorff convergence and obtain an explicit approximation estimate. These spectral compressions are length-filtered Peter--Weyl truncations of the compact dual. The resulting regular bi-invariant Lip-norm also places the family within Leimbach's operator Gromov--Hausdorff convergence theorem. The construction applies to non-unimodular discrete quantum groups, including discrete duals of standard deformations of compact semisimple Lie groups.

papers.title: Approximate $K$-Conjugacy of Minimal Cantor--Circle Extensions I: The Rigid Case
papers.abstract: We study approximate $K$-conjugacy for minimal Cantor--circle extensions with arbitrary circle homeomorphism cocycles, allowing orientation reversal. Under the assumption of classical rigidity, we show that two such systems are approximately $K$-conjugate if and only if there exists an ordered unital graded $K$-theory isomorphism satisfying the finite coefficient $K$-condition. Our approach combines dynamical corrections along Kakutani--Rokhlin towers with the classification and uniqueness theory of $C^*$-algebras. Moreover, the crossed-product isomorphisms implementing approximate $K$-conjugacy can be chosen as inner perturbations of a fixed isomorphism and its inverse.

papers.title: Kadison's open problem and $R^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: We study $R^*$-subalgebras of von Neumann algebras. In finite homogeneous type $\mathrm I_n$, every $R^*$-subalgebra is locally finite-dimensional. We also give a trace criterion for local finite dimensionality in the semifinite setting under a finite-trace hypothesis, and prove an approximate halving property for projections in strongly dense $R^*$-subalgebras of type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factors. For three projections in an $R^*$-subalgebra of a type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor, the reduced word-length filtration gives bounds on layer growth, criteria for stabilization, and uniform bounds on minimal-polynomial degrees at each fixed word length. Finally, we give a negative answer to Kadison's fifteenth problem by constructing an infinite-dimensional unital $*$-algebra generated algebraically by three projections in which every selfadjoint element has finite spectrum. The resulting $R^*$-algebra embeds unitally into every type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor.

papers.title: Infinite projections and failure of pure infiniteness in simple nuclear $C^*$-algebras
papers.abstract: We construct a separable, unital, simple, nuclear $C^*$-algebra in the UCT class such that every nonzero projection in its stabilization is infinite, while it contains a nonzero projectionless hereditary subalgebra. The construction gives a negative answer to the question whether infiniteness of all nonzero projections in a unital simple nuclear $C^*$-algebra implies pure infiniteness.

papers.title: Quasi-locality and weak containment for Roe algebras
papers.abstract: We establish two characterisations of Property A for discrete metric spaces of bounded geometry. Such a space has Property A if and only if its Roe algebra coincides with its quasi-local algebra, and if and only if the canonical map from its maximal Roe algebra to its reduced Roe algebra is injective. Both characterisations hold in the uniform and ordinary Roe settings. We also prove, without assuming Property A, that strong quasi-locality is equivalent to norm approximability by finite-propagation operators. In particular, the strongly quasi-local algebra always coincides with the Roe algebra. As applications, we show that a discrete group is exact whenever its full group $C^*$-algebra has the local lifting property, and that the maximal injective crossed-product functor agrees with the reduced crossed-product functor precisely for exact discrete groups.

papers.title: Generalised diagonal dimension and applications to large-scale geometry
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce a generalised diagonal dimension. We explain why the generalised diagonal dimension extends the notion of diagonal dimension defined by Li, Liao, and Winter, and under which conditions these dimensions coincide. We prove permanence properties for the generalised diagonal dimension and compare it with the nuclear dimension. We investigate applications of the generalised diagonal dimension in large-scale geometry; specifically, we show that the generalised diagonal dimension of a noncommutative Cartan subalgebra in the C*-algebra generated by finite-propagation operators on a uniformly locally finite metric space is bounded above by the asymptotic dimension of the space, and we conjecture that the two are equal.

papers.title: Quantum Gromov--Hausdorff Convergence of Spectral Truncations for Compact Quantum Groups with Proper Length Functions
papers.abstract: We study the quantum Gromov--Hausdorff convergence of spectral truncations of \(C(G)\), where \(G\) is a coamenable compact quantum group equipped with a proper length function. Using higher-order commutator seminorms, we establish sufficient conditions for the induced Lipschitz seminorms to define compact quantum metric structures. Furthermore, for the Dirac operators associated with the length function, we prove that their spectral truncations converge to the original space in the quantum Gromov--Hausdorff distance. Our results apply to \(SU(N)\), \(SO(N)\), and related examples, including coamenable compact quantum groups of Kac type with polynomial growth.

papers.title: A solution to Haagerup's Problem on decomposable maps
papers.abstract: We prove that a von Neumann algebra $N$ is injective if and only if $\|T\|_{\mathrm{dec}}=\|T\|_{\mathrm{cb}}$ for every linear map $T:\ell^\infty_3\to N$, answering a problem of Haagerup (1985).
